title_en: Reply of the Supreme People's Court on the Issue of Whether a Credit Cooperative Shall Bear Civil Liability for Causing Losses to Others by Violating Prescribed Procedures in Handling Remittance Reversal

articles.content_en:
Supreme People's Court
Reply on the Issue of Whether a Credit Cooperative Shall Bear Civil Liability for Causing Losses to Others by Handling Return of Remittance in Violation of Regulations
Fa (Jing) Fu [1988] No. 45
Higher People's Court of Hubei Province:
We have received your request for instruction No. E Gao (1988) Jing Zi No. 25. With regard to the issue of whether a credit cooperative that handles return of remittance in violation of the “Measures for Settlement of Accounts of the People’s Bank of China” shall participate in litigation as a subject of action and bear civil liability for the losses caused, upon study, we reply as follows:
On December 12, 1985, Hubei Province Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Industry Joint Company remitted 92,000 yuan by telegraph as payment for goods to the Gao Dian Zi Town Purchasing Station in Jianshi County, Hubei Province. Later, because the purchasing station had no goods available, the two parties went to Hua Yuan Xiang Credit Cooperative on January 3, 1986, to handle the remittance return procedures. The credit cooperative collected remittance fees, settled all interest on the payment, and issued a remittance certificate bearing the credit cooperative’s official seal and the private seal of its responsible person, stating “Return of remittance of 92,036.70 yuan by the purchasing station to Hubei Province Agriculture, Animal Husbandry and Industry Joint Company.” The certificate was taken back to Wuhan by the Joint Company. On January 4 of the same year, the purchasing station went alone to Hua Yuan Xiang Credit Cooperative to request cancellation of the remittance. The responsible person of the credit cooperative cancelled the remittance without recovering the original remittance certificate. The purchasing station then divided and used the funds, causing economic losses to the Joint Company.
Hua Yuan Xiang Credit Cooperative violated the provisions of Item 7 of Article 10 of the “Measures for Settlement of Accounts of the People’s Bank of China,” which stipulates: “When a remitting unit requests a return of remittance for a remitted amount, it shall prepare a formal letter and bring the original remittance receipt to the remitting bank to apply for return.” The credit cooperative not only failed to remit the payment to the payee in a timely manner, but also handled the return of remittance procedures without recovering the remittance certificate it had issued and without the applicant’s complete formalities, thereby causing economic losses to the payee, the Joint Company. According to the provisions of Paragraph 1 and Paragraph 2 of Article 106 of the “General Principles of the Civil Law of the People’s Republic of China,” the credit cooperative may be named as a litigant in the action and shall bear civil liability according to law.
Hereby reply.
October 18, 1988
